source.study: Migratory birds advance spring arrival and egg-laying in the Arctic, mostly by travelling faster
source.transport_amendment: browser file_stream endpoint returned 403 to GitHub Actions; public Dryad API download endpoint substituted before any numerical outcome was observed

question: Across independent Arctic-breeding migratory bird populations, does individual timing dispersion and rank at departure persist, contract, or amplify by Arctic-circle arrival and breeding arrival?

primary_analysis.inclusion: complete depart and AC; population-year groups with at least 3 complete migrations
primary_analysis.estimator: pooled within-group OLS slope AC_centered ~ depart_centered
primary_analysis.uncertainty: 10000-replicate cluster bootstrap by individual_id, resampling whole individual histories
primary_analysis.interpretation: individual departure timing differences are contracted rather than fully retained by Arctic-circle arrival

secondary_transitions.inclusion: complete AC and arrival; population-year groups n>=3
complete arrival and nest.initiation; population-year groups n>=3
complete depart and arrival; population-year groups n>=3

variance_funnel.role: second serial signature; not sufficient alone to prove feedback

actuator_diagnostics.caveat: travel_speed is partly mechanically related to travel duration and is therefore a supportive actuator diagnostic, not an independent causal test
descriptive only; stopovers.f availability may vary among taxa

population_heterogeneity.rule: estimate population-specific depart->AC lambda only when n_complete>=20, >=3 years, and within-group departure variance >0
population_heterogeneity.role: descriptive heterogeneity; no universal lambda and no ranking of taxa by biological correction strength

direct_serial_decomposition.role: prospective descriptive application of serial theorem

forbidden: call departure timing a physiological readiness measurement
infer molecular clocks from departure dates
treat travel_speed compensation as independent of the timing interval used to calculate travel_speed
claim all species share one biological lambda
use this dataset to confirm the post-hoc serial two-clock theorem without labeling it an independent post-theory test
retune frozen GEB V2 or preregistered outcomes
